cards.hint: Think about order of building blocks
options: determining the order of the four chemical building blocks
turning genes on or off with regulatory instructions
threading single strands through tiny pores in a membrane
watching polymerase molecules with a fast movie camera
cards.quote: Sequencing DNA means determining the order of the four chemical building blocks - called "bases" - that make up the DNA molecule.
cards.stem: What does sequencing DNA mean for scientists studying a molecule?

cards.hint: Recall the size mentioned for quick cheap comparison
options: 1 million bases or more
3 billion base pairs
30 cancer types
cards.quote: Researchers now are able to compare large stretches of DNA - 1 million bases or more - from different individuals quickly and cheaply.
cards.stem: What can researchers now do with large stretches of DNA from different people?

cards.hint: Think about choosing treatments for a specific cancer type
options: identify the particular type of cancer a patient has
study the same molecule over and over again
screen newborns for disease and disease risk
compare inheritance in response to environmental influences
cards.quote: In cancer, for example, physicians are increasingly able to use sequence data to identify the particular type of cancer a patient has.
cards.stem: In cancer care, what are physicians increasingly able to do with sequence data?

cards.hint: Focus on what the order reveals about a segment
options: the kind of genetic information that is carried in a particular DNA segment
the pairing that copies molecules when cells divide
the details of some common and complex diseases
cards.quote: The sequence tells scientists the kind of genetic information that is carried in a particular DNA segment.
cards.stem: What do scientists learn from reading the order of bases?
